walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 2: Composing — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 2: Composing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 2: Composing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets equal a semibreve?
A dot after a note adds?
options: A quarter of its value
A half of its value
A full extra
A double value

mcqs.q: What is a tone row in serial music?
options: Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
Classical means any old serious music.
A row of notes played together as a chord.
An ordered series of all 12 chromatic pitches, used as the basis of a piece.
Three different sections (ABC).
Music in 3/4 time.
Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
Three sections: A, contrasting B, and a return to A (ABA).

mcqs.q: What distinguishes Classical (1750-1820) from Baroque style?
options: Clearer melodic phrases, homophonic texture, balanced structures like sonata form.
Music in 3/4 time.
Classical means any old serious music.
Use of orchestra (Baroque had none).
